sense: set fire to; hurt with heat

evidence: Verg. A. 7.13: ūrit odōrātam nocturna in lūmina cedrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The general verb: to burn something, and of fire, heat or the sun, to burn or scorch someone. Short u in ustum, as the lexicon writes adustus for now.

evidence: Caes. B.G. 1.5.2: oppida sua omnia … incendunt (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Sen. 84: cujus ā mē corpus est cremātum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of things burnt to nothing, books, rubbish, a city; above all of burning the dead.

phrases.latin: calidum hoc est: etsī procul abest, ūrit male.
phrases.english: this is hot: even from a distance it burns badly.
Mind you don’t burn your fingers.

sources: Lewis & Short: uro · Lewis & Short: incendo · Lewis & Short: cremo
